display.purpose: Page h1s and the large Package price.

headline.purpose: Section h2s, the homepage tagline and Package names.

title.purpose: Rental names, booking step titles, the viewer caption on a phone; Setup captions at line-height 1.3.

body.purpose: All running text, at most 65ch per line.

label.purpose: Hints, errors and copyright; menu links and the phone Menu button add 0.04em tracking; the sample tag is uppercase with 0.08em.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The settling ease-out every arrival uses: reveals, the menu panel, the Photo viewer opening, the link line drawing out.

motion.name: duration-press
motion.purpose: A pill or Setup card settling to 0.98 as it is pressed.

motion.name: duration-exit
motion.purpose: Something leaving or closing (menu panel, Photo viewer, filtered-out cards), and hover colour fades on links and pills.

motion.name: duration-open
motion.purpose: An overlay or menu opening, the menu icon folding into an ×, the link line drawing out.

motion.name: duration-rise
motion.purpose: Content rising 1.5rem and fading into view on load or first scroll.

motion.name: duration-linger
motion.purpose: A Gallery card's photo easing to 1.04 inside its arch on hover or focus.

motion.name: duration-settle
motion.purpose: A photo settling from 1.06 to full size inside its arch as it is revealed.

motion.name: stagger
motion.purpose: Between things arriving together, capped at four steps.

motion.name: duration-turn
motion.purpose: One turn of the thin arc in Contact's Send pill while an Inquiry is sending.

narrative.overview:
Likha Events is a designer's studio, not a party store. The site should read like the atelier's own portfolio: warm off-white paper, charcoal ink, a single forest-green voice for action, and the brand's arch framing each Setup like a piece on the studio wall. The customer's own colours and themes are what fill the arches, so the frame around them stays composed and quiet, and each Setup's colours carry the page.

The system is light and airy, not dense. Sections breathe on a generous vertical rhythm, alternating paper with soft sage bands. A high-contrast serif (Cormorant Garamond) carries headings, captions and prices with an atelier's flourish, and a clean geometric sans (Jost) keeps everything else plain and readable. Components are soft and assured: thin hairlines, generous padding, curves wherever the arch allows, and one solid green action at a time.

The site avoids the party-store look: no bright primaries, confetti, bubbly display type or busy pattern backgrounds. When a Setup is bold and colourful, the photo is allowed to be loud, and the frame stays calm around it.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white paper and charcoal ink, with forest green reserved for actions, links and prices.
The arch (a semicircular top over a 4:5 portrait) frames every featured photo.
A serif for headings, captions and prices, a sans for everything else.
Flat surfaces. Depth comes from tone (paper vs. sage band) and hairlines, never shadows.
Pill-shaped buttons and filter chips that echo the arch's curve.
Slow, restrained motion in transform and opacity only, settling on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) and switched off under "reduce motion". Every page has it.

rules.name: The Sage Is Not Ink Rule
rules.body: The brand sage (sage) never carries text. Wherever the brand guide says "sage band", the band is sage-band and the text on it stays charcoal or forest.

rules.name: The One Green Voice Rule
rules.body: Forest marks things you can act on, plus prices. A paragraph, heading or decoration is never forest just to add colour.

rules.name: The AA Pairing Rule
rules.body: Every text colour on every background meets WCAG AA (4.5:1). A new pairing is checked before it ships, and its ratio is noted beside the token in tokens.css.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks for the Studio Rule
rules.body: The serif is for headings, captions, prices and the tagline. Labels, form text, buttons and navigation use the sans.

rules.name: The Medium Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings sit at weight 500. Cormorant gets heavier quickly, so don't go bolder for emphasis. Use size or a sage-band setting instead.

rules.name: The Paper and Mist Rule
rules.body: Lift something by moving it onto or off a sage band, or by giving it a hairline. Don't add drop shadows.

rules.name: The Arch Frames the Work Rule
rules.body: Any photo of Likha Events' work shown as a single feature goes in an arch. The Photo viewer is the exception, because it shows the whole photo uncropped, matted like a print.

dos: Do put every featured photo of a Setup or Rental in the arch (4:5 aspect, rounded.arch), cropped by CSS with object-fit: cover.
Do use the custom properties in src/styles/tokens.css for colour, type, space and --radius. Add a new token there, with its contrast ratio noted, rather than writing a new one-off value.
Do keep one solid forest pill as the main action in each place, with outline pills or text links for anything beside it.
Do separate sections with paper and sage bands and 1px hairlines.
Do let the photos carry the colour. The frame around them stays paper, ink and green.
Do keep touch targets at least 44px tall and every page free of sideways scrolling at 375px.
Do write any motion with transform and opacity only (hover and focus colour fades aside), on the motion tokens, slow and restrained, and turn it all off under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use sage for text, or put text on a full-strength sage background.
Don't add drop shadows, gradients or glows to cards or buttons.
Don't add a party-store look: bright primary colours, confetti, balloon clip art, bubbly or script display fonts, or pattern backgrounds.
Don't set headings bolder than 500, or set labels, buttons or form text in the serif.
Don't add new rectangular buttons. Calls to action are pills.
Don't alter or re-crop the stored photos. Framing happens in CSS.
